questions.learningObjective: Explain why a water depth is charted as shallower than the surveyed depth
questions.stem: Projection note PN-01 records that a surveyed river depth of 3 m is charted as a shallower value for the surface projection.

options.text: Because light bends away from the normal on leaving the water, so the riverbed appears nearer the surface
Because the water absorbs the red end of the light, so the bed cannot be seen accurately
options.misconception: blames absorption rather than refraction

options.text: Because the chart projection always exaggerates depth in the upstream direction
options.misconception: attributes the shift to the projection convention

options.text: Because refraction in the air above the water shifts the bed further from the observer
options.misconception: puts the refraction in the wrong medium

questions.explanation: Light from the riverbed bends away from the normal on leaving the water, so the observer traces it back to a point nearer the surface. The charted depth is therefore smaller than the true depth.
questions.hint: Apparent depth is less than the real depth.

options.text: Because the prism is made of coloured glass that filters one band out of the white light
options.misconception: believes the prism contains dyes

options.text: Because the refractive index of glass differs slightly for each wavelength, so each colour bends differently
Because the prism surface is rough enough to scatter the light into separate colours
options.misconception: explains the spectrum by scattering

options.text: Because the white light is already a mixture of coloured rays that the prism only separates
options.misconception: overstates what the prism does

questions.explanation: Glass has a different refractive index for each wavelength, so the prism bends each colour by a different amount. Violet bends most and red least, and the white beam emerges as a spectrum.

options.text: Because the glass has to push the light along, so it loses energy at each surface
options.misconception: explains the delay by pushing

options.text: Because the denser medium holds the wave back through repeated interactions with the atoms
Because the glass converts some of the light into heat, so the remainder moves more slowly
options.misconception: confuses absorption with the speed of light

options.text: Because the light bends at the entry surface and the bend consumes the speed
options.misconception: believes bending slows the light

questions.explanation: Light's speed depends on the medium's response. In glass the oscillating atoms delay the field, so the speed falls to about c/n, roughly 2 times 10 to the 8 metres per second.

options.misconception: claims one colour is blocked

options.misconception: insists on a real image

questions.topic: Minimum deviation of a prism
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the angle of minimum deviation of a prism
questions.stem: QA note PN-27 asks for the angle of minimum deviation of a prism of index 1.5 with an apex angle of 60 degrees.
questions.explanation: The minimum deviation satisfies n = sin((A + D)/2) divided by sin(A/2), so D = 2 arcsin(n sin(A/2)) - A = 2 arcsin(0.75) - 60 = 37.2 degrees. The ray path is symmetric at that setting.
questions.hint: Use D = 2 arcsin of n sin A/2, minus A.

options.text: Because a thin prism has a smaller refractive index for every colour

Because a thin prism spreads the light further, so the colours separate more
options.misconception: reverses the effect of a small angle

questions.explanation: For a thin prism the deviation is roughly (n - 1)A, so a smaller apex angle gives a proportionally smaller colour separation. Using a thicker prism is effectively enlarging that angle.
